body:
### Question

Hi! I wanted to enforce some environments to always be satisfied for my project and initially I've added them to `required-environments`. A bit of a problem I've noticed that it doesn't prevent unrelated platform wheels from appearing the lockfile, so I've also added the same environments to `environments`. And then I've noticed that removing `required-environments` still keeps environments required.

Steps to reproduce:
1. `uv init .`
2. `uv add --no-sync pywin32`
3, Add `tool.uv` below.
```
[tool.uv]
# Require that the package is available on the following platforms:
environments = [
    # macOS on Apple Silicon (ARM)
    "sys_platform == 'darwin' and platform_machine == 'arm64'",
    # Linux on x86_64 (Intel/AMD)
    "sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'x86_64'",
    # Windows on x86_64 (Intel/AMD)
    "sys_platform == 'win32' and platform_machine == 'AMD64'",
]
```
4. `uv lock`.

Results in 
```
error: No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers: platform_machine == 'arm64' and sys_platform == 'darwin')
  cause: Because pywin32==312 has no `platform_machine == 'arm64' and sys_platform == 'darwin'`-compatible wheels and only pywin32<=312 is available, we can conclude that pywin32>=312 cannot be used.
         And because your project depends on pywin32>=312, we can conclude that your project's requirements are unsatisfiable.

```
So effectively just using `environments` is enough to enforce required environments. Is this expected? This does seems to contract the docs (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/settings/#required-environments):

> While the environments setting limits the set of environments that uv will consider when resolving dependencies, required-environments expands the set of platforms that uv must support when resolving dependencies.
> 
> For example, environments = ["sys_platform == 'darwin'"] would limit uv to solving for macOS (and ignoring Linux and Windows). On the other hand, required-environments = ["sys_platform == 'darwin'"] would require that any package without a source distribution include a wheel for macOS in order to be installable.

Which sounds like adding `environments` shouldn't make resolution fail.

### Platform

-

### Version

uv 0.13.8
title: `tool.uv.environments` also acts as `required-environments`
